question: Two trains having lengths of 340 m and 360 m are running at speeds of 80 km/h and 90 km/h, respectively, in the same direction. The time taken (in minutes) by the faster train, coming from behind, to completely cross the other train is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed of trains in the same direction = 90 − 80 = 10 km/h.

Convert to m/s: 10 × (5/18) = 25/9 m/s.

Total distance to cross = Length of both trains = 340 + 360 = 700 m.

Time taken = Distance ÷ Relative Speed = 700 × (9/25) = 252 seconds.

Convert time to minutes = 252 ÷ 60 = 4.2 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.2 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the faster train (L₁) = 360 m

Length of the slower train (L₂) = 340 m

Speed of the faster train (S₁) = 90 km/h

Speed of the slower train (S₂) = 80 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (Same Direction) = S₁ − S₂

Time Taken = Total Length ÷ Relative Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Length to cross = L₁ + L₂ = 360 + 340 = 700 m

⇒ Relative Speed = 90 − 80 = 10 km/h

⇒ Convert relative speed to m/s = 10 × (5/18) = 25/9 m/s

⇒ Time Taken (in seconds) = 700 ÷ (25/9)

⇒ Time Taken = (700 × 9) ÷ 25

⇒ Time Taken = 28 × 9 = 252 seconds

⇒ Convert seconds to minutes = 252 ÷ 60 = 4.2 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 4.2 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two objects travel in the same direction, their relative speed is calculated by taking the difference of their individual speeds: Relative Speed = S₁ − S₂.

Relative Speed in Opposite Directions

When two objects travel towards each other in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂.

Distance Covered in Train Crossings

When a train completely crosses another moving or stationary train, a platform, or a bridge, the total distance covered is always the sum of both their lengths (L₁ + L₂).

Speed Conversions

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply the speed by 5/18. To convert m/s back to km/h, multiply by 18/5.
